sehemu: Part II: Consolidated Fund and Finances of the United Republic
jina: Controller and Auditor-General of the United Republic
maudhui: (1) There shall be a Controller and Auditor-General of the United Republic. (2) The Controller and Auditor-General shall be responsible for: (a) ensuring that money proposed to be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund has been authorized and will be withdrawn in accordance with Article 136, and, when satisfied, authorizing its withdrawal; (b) ensuring that all money authorized to be charged upon the Consolidated Fund or appropriated by an Act of Parliament and expended has been applied to the purposes for which it was authorized and in accordance with the authority granted; and (c) at least once every year auditing and reporting on the accounts of the Government of the United Republic, accounts administered by public officers of that Government, accounts of all courts of the United Republic and accounts administered by the Clerk of the National Assembly. (3) The Controller and Auditor-General and every public officer authorized by him shall have access to all books, records, statements, reports and other documents relating to accounts referred to in subarticle (2). (4) The Controller and Auditor-General shall submit to the President every report made under subarticle (2). After receiving it, the President shall cause it to be laid before the first sitting of Parliament held thereafter and within seven days after that sitting begins. If the President does not cause the report to be laid before Parliament, the Controller and Auditor-General shall submit it to the Speaker, or Deputy Speaker where appropriate, who shall lay it before Parliament. (5) The Controller and Auditor-General shall also perform such other functions and exercise such other powers as may be prescribed by law in relation to accounts of the Government of the United Republic, public authorities or corporations. (6) In exercising powers under subarticles (2), (3) and (4), the Controller and Auditor-General shall not be subject to the direction or control of any other person or Government department, without prejudice to the jurisdiction of a court to determine whether those powers have been exercised in accordance with this Constitution.

(3) The Controller and Auditor-General and every public officer authorized by him shall have access to all books, records, statements, reports and other documents relating to accounts referred to in subarticle (2).
